English Wikipedia says outright that it is unknown when the Longyou caves were created: pots dated to 206 BC-23 AD were found in silt inside them (a latest-possible date, since the silt came after the digging), the first written mention is a 17th-century poem, and the figure 'more than 2000 years old' is only a lower bound. Ancient Origins repeats 'at least 2,000 years'; Chinese Wikipedia gives a Western Han start (Emperor Xuan granaries) as the view of one researcher and calls it a single opinion with riddles unsolved. No source dates the start of the excavation to a year, century or period, and the stored -500 is the band edge a rule wrote, so the start stays undated. The Icknield Way is an ancient trackway whose age is disputed: the Wikipedia article says only that the route existed 'at least as early as the Iron Age' (a lower bound on existence, not a start) and that its prehistoric origin 'has been questioned'; the earliest documentary mentions are Anglo-Saxon charters of 903. Other readings range from Neolithic to a formalised ditched road of about 100 BC in North Hertfordshire. No readable source dates the start of the route itself.
